active.body:
The most recent Rubin data `tocsin` has reached is MJD 61249.42, which is 94.4 days behind now. The broker mirror normally lags ~16 days; the limit here is 30.

The channel itself is fine — it is running on schedule and committing results. What has stopped is the DATA. A screen re-reading the same frontier every night produces a clean null indefinitely and looks healthy from every other angle, which is why this check exists separately from the staleness check.

Check whether ALeRCE is still ingesting the LSST alert stream before reading any recent null from this channel.

**Cause established 2026-10-26 by `rubin-outage`: SKY_STOPPED.** Independent brokers stop on the same night (ALeRCE 2026-07-14; fink 2026-07-14), so the alert stream itself stopped and no change to the broker path recovers data that was never taken. Do not relax the threshold on this — the condition is real. See `docs/rubin-outage.md`. ZTF, the other public wide-field alert stream, is LIVE (newest night 2026-10-26 via alerce_ztf), so `tocsin-altfeeds` has a current feed to lean on.

`loom` has reported the same newest epoch, MJD 61235.41627, on every run since 2026-07-30T13:13:46Z — 92.3 days, against a limit of 7. Source: `results/loom/screen.json` → `frontier_mjd`.

The frontier has not yet been observed to advance at all, so there is no measured cadence to compare this against.

The channel is running and committing normally; what has stopped is the mirror. Every null it reports while this holds means *no new sky*, not *clean sky*, and the two are not the same result.

Check whether ALeRCE is still ingesting the LSST alert stream. If the pause turns out to be ordinary batching, raise `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` using the cadence recorded in `results/alerts/frontier.json` rather than by guessing again.

**Cause established 2026-10-26 by `rubin-outage`: SKY_STOPPED.** Independent brokers stop on the same night (ALeRCE 2026-07-14; fink 2026-07-14), so the alert stream itself stopped and no change to the broker path recovers data that was never taken. Do not relax the threshold on this — the condition is real. See `docs/rubin-outage.md`. ZTF, the other public wide-field alert stream, is LIVE (newest night 2026-10-26 via alerce_ztf), so `tocsin-altfeeds` has a current feed to lean on.

active.body:
`tocsin` has advanced from MJD 61235.41918 to MJD 61343.30987 — 107.9 days of sky — after sitting still since 2026-07-30T10:26:40Z.

The stall was confirmed across 91.5 days of sightings; the advance itself happened between 2026-10-29T21:44:10Z and now, so the interval between successive frontier values is 92.4 days. That is an UPPER BOUND on the mirror's true ingest gap — this repository samples the frontier about once a day and cannot see a change finer than that.

The frontier is now 0.5 days behind the wall clock, inside the 30-day limit, so the age alert clears. That is not the same as current: the mirror's ordinary lag is ~16 days, and anything above that is still backlog.

This is the cadence datum `FRONTIER_STALL_DAYS` has never had — it was set to 7 by guesswork because no advance had ever been observed here. Recalibrate it against `observed_advance_days` in `results/alerts/frontier.json` now that there is one.

Note that the nights lost to the stall are ABSENT, not null: they were never observed, so they add nothing to the screen's trial count and must not be counted as clean sky.
active.title: TOCSIN's data frontier is moving again (+107.9 days of sky)
